title: Conformal Prediction at Performative Equilibrium: The Price of Performativity
abstract: Conformal prediction gives finite-sample coverage when calibration and test points are exchangeable, but exchangeability can fail when deployment changes the data distribution. We study conformal prediction in performative settings, where the deployed predictor affects the data distribution, and seek prediction sets valid at performative equilibrium: coverage must hold under $D(f^\star)$ for a performatively stable predictor $f^\star$. Under total-variation $L$-sensitivity of the distribution map, we prove a phase transition at $L=1$. If $L \ge 1$, no finite-sample procedure can uniformly guarantee both equilibrium-valid coverage and nontrivial prediction sets. If $L<1$, the minimax excess miscoverage over informative procedures is $\widetildeΩ(1/((1-L)\sqrt{n}))$, implying a sample-complexity inflation of order $1/(1-L)^2$ for fixed excess miscoverage. Our main technical tool is a transfer theorem: any procedure returning a predictor within $\varepsilon$ of equilibrium yields equilibrium-valid coverage up to an additive $L\varepsilon$ term after split-conformal calibration. We instantiate the theorem with two retraining algorithms: a model-free method for discretizable classes and a parametric tail-averaged method that matches the $n$- and $L$-dependence of this rate up to logarithmic factors. Experiments, including semi-synthetic credit scoring, demonstrate the predicted threshold behavior and scaling laws.

We study conformal prediction in performative settings, where the deployed predictor affects the data Distribution .

title: De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes
abstract: We attempt to alleviate failure modes of classical physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in scenarios of topological pathologies corresponding to punctures, holes, poles, and voids by introducing de Rham cohomological augmentations, or Hodge-de Rham PINNs. Vanilla PINNs often encounter pitfalls in hole-based settings due to discontinuous interfaces, nonzero closed path integration, path dependence, correspondence to exact forms via the exterior derivative, etc., therefore we absolve traditional failures via parameterizing a 1-form by the Hodge-Morrey-Friedrichs (HMF) decomposition for manifolds with boundary, drawing a connection to de Rham cohomology such as through the HMF isomorphism theorem. 1-forms can act as representations of scalar-valued PDE solutions through integral operator mappings. We propose performing a PINN-based loss on the parameterized 1-form through an associated PDE, which subsequently solves the potential-based PINN problem and moreover remedies the failures of vanilla PINNs via the Sobolev-regular operator under a Fréchet differentiation interconnection. The operator relationship often has a nontrivial closed-form and often requires integration or a case-by-case analysis, which we address thoroughly in our experiments. When an integrability condition is not met on our losses, we can equip exhaustion functions to train the networks. We demonstrate our methods on the Aharonov-Bohm effect, which, to our understanding, is largely nonexistent in PINN literature. We develop theoretical guarantees of our methods and demonstrate our pathological safeguards on a broad selection of topologically-adverse problems, including scenarios of inexact forms, and those of nontrivial harmonics and coexact terms.
ai_summary: Vanilla PINNs often encounter pitfalls in hole-based settings due to discontinuous interfaces, nonzero closed path integration, path dependence, and path dependence . We propose performing a PINN-based loss on the parameterized 1-form through an associated PDE, which subsequently solves the potential-based PINN problem .

title: Route Anything: A Study of Model and Policy Routing for General-Purpose AI Systems
abstract: Artificial general intelligence (AGI) requires a method that can understand, generate, reason, and act across diverse domains and modalities. Rather than relying on a single model to master every capability, a promising path toward AGI now is to orchestrate a heterogeneous ecosystem of specialized models, tools, and policies (candidates) into a unified AI system. At the heart of this vision lies a fundamental question: how can an AI system dynamically select and coordinate the most capable candidate for each task while balancing performance and computational cost? In this work, we present Route Anything, a unified framework for studying model and policy routing across general-purpose AI systems. We develop a unified theoretical foundation that characterizes optimal routing under quality--cost trade-offs and establishes how the information available to a router determines its attainable performance. To systematically investigate routing across diverse capabilities, we first construct an omni-modal trajectory matrix spanning 25 benchmarks across language understanding, image, video, and speech generation, coding and workplace agents, and robotic manipulation, comprising 374,401 scored runs from 452 candidate configurations. Building on this framework, we train and test different routers to investigate the potential of omni-modal model routing, the capabilities of learned routers, and the conditions under which routing improves efficiency. Our results reveal substantial opportunities for capability orchestration: per-input oracle routing outperforms the best fixed candidate by 5.4 points, and learned routers outperform it by 0.3 points across 16 benchmarks, by 2.1 points on video generation, and by 1.1 points on robot manipulation while using 24% less policy time. More importantly, routing raises efficiency by 8.82x on average compared with the reference model.
ai_summary: A promising path toward AGI is to orchestrate a heterogeneous ecosystem of specialized models, tools, and policies into a unified AI system . At the heart of this vision lies a fundamental question: how can an AI system dynamically select and coordinate the most capable candidate for each task while balancing performance and computational cost?

title: The Geometry of Ignorance: Detecting Suppressed Knowledge in LLMs through Activation Fragmentation
abstract: Evaluating whether a large language model (LLM) genuinely knows a concept remains a fundamental problem, since behavioral metrics can be fooled by suppression: a model that refuses to answer may still harbor recoverable knowledge. The framework measures the geometric coherence of \textit{anon-vectors}, the differences in hidden states between a concept-specific query and its anonymized paraphrase, and shows that genuine knowledge forms a tight, low-entropy cluster while ignorance forces geometric fragmentation. Across ten instruction-tuned LLMs from three model families, all fragmentation metrics reliably separate known from unknown concepts, and post-unlearning, fragmentation geometry correlates with adversarial recovery across four attack types and five unlearning algorithms, though the direction of that relationship is shown to depend on attack methodology. Furthermore, a layer-resolved analysis reveals that different adversarial mechanisms exploit this geometry at varying depths, with high attack-specific correlations that are invisible to behavioral evaluation. Together, these results constitute a single-phase, attack-free proxy for unlearning robustness that captures aspects of parametric knowledge inaccessible to output-level metrics. A reference implementation is available at https://github.com/AdarPeleg/geometry-of-ignorance
ai_summary: The framework measures the geometric coherence of \textit{anon-vectors}, the differences in hidden states between a concept-specific query and its anonymized paraphrase . The framework shows that genuine knowledge forms a tight, low-entropy cluster while ignorance forces geometric fragmentation .

title: iGC: Antibody Optimization via Reinforcement Learning over a Learned Somatic Hypermutation Prior
abstract: Antibody affinity maturation is a natural optimization process in which B cells acquire mutations through somatic hypermutation (SHM), undergo selection for improved antigen binding, and iteratively evolve toward higher affinity. Computationally modeling this process requires capturing both biologically plausible mutations and antigen-specific selection. However, existing mutation models do not directly optimize binding, while affinity optimization often neglects realistic mutation trajectories. We introduce iGC (in silico Germinal Centers), a two-stage reinforcement learning (RL) framework for antigen-specific antibody optimization. Stage 1 learns an SHM mutation prior from parent-child pairs in B-cell lineage trees and adapts it to a target affinity-maturation dataset. Stage 2 initializes an RL policy from this prior and optimizes antigen binding with Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization toward the frozen prior. To prevent reward exploitation, including repetitive high-reward substitutions and structurally tolerated framework mutations, we introduce a Reward-Tax Meta-Gradient objective. RewardNet smooths the affinity landscape, while TaxNet penalizes reward overexploitation, jointly defining a learned meta-reward for policy optimization. We evaluate iGC on mutation prediction, SHM consistency, affinity optimization, and mutation diversity. The mutation prior more than doubles the strongest baseline in mutation-site prediction. Following RL optimization, iGC maintains SHM sequence structure. It also achieves a strong exploration-exploitation balance, yielding competitive reward-diversity products across candidate-selection cutoffs. These results demonstrate that iGC integrates biologically plausible mutation generation with antigen-specific affinity selection, providing an in silico framework for iterative antibody affinity maturation.

title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Naive on-policy RL is often bottlenecked by the capabilities of the base model --- insufficient coverage can result in an inability to learn from certain rewards. At the same time, rewards in modern post-training systems often come from rich textual sources, e.g. judge models with a rubric of criteria. Can we utilize such structures to provide a rich directional signal that enables improving on otherwise difficult to optimize rewards? In this work, we examine a framework we refer to as targeted guidance that learns from per-turn textual feedback via an on-policy self-distillation objective. Our focus is not only on directly improving hard-to-optimize behaviors, but on how to do so throughout the training process without degrading baseline RL performance. Over a range of settings across an agentic multi-turn software engineering environment, we find success by combining targeted self-distillation with a per-criteria RL reward, and by limiting feedback to turns where the policy specifically fails. We further examine the design choices that lead to stable entropy and reduce oscillatory behavior throughout training.
ai_summary: Naive on-policy RL is often bottlenecked by the capabilities of the base model . insufficient coverage can result in an inability to learn from certain rewards . At the same time, rewards in modern post-training systems often come from rich textual sources .

title: Gaussian Partitioning for Reliable Learning of Multi-Index Models
abstract: We introduce Gaussian partitioning, an algorithmic primitive for distributions smooth with respect to a Gaussian. It partitions space into polyhedral regions so that almost all mass lies in thin strips restricting a few orthogonal directions. Within each strip, the conditional distribution approximately matches low-degree Gaussian moments in the unrestricted directions. Our construction builds on logconcave partitioning of Diakonikolas, Kane, and Ma (FOCS 2026). Under input marginals smooth with respect to the standard Gaussian, we obtain agnostic learners with error $(1+c)\mathrm{opt}+ε$ for broad classes of Boolean multi-index models, including functions of halfspaces, low-dimensional convex concepts, and low-dimensional polynomial threshold functions. For functions of $k$ halfspaces, both agnostic and testable agnostic learners achieve this error with dimension dependence $d^{\mathrm{poly}(k/c)}$, improving the previous exponential dependence on $k/c$ in the agnostic exponent. For learning from positive examples with imperfect unlabeled data (PUI), we give algorithms and Statistical Query (SQ) lower bounds that qualitatively characterize complexity through Gaussian moment matching. For fixed smoothness and positive-mass parameters, we learn intersections of $k$ halfspaces with dimension dependence $d^{O(\log(k/ε))}$ and matching SQ lower bounds, improving the previous $d^{\mathrm{poly}(1/ε)}$ upper bound even for one halfspace. A general reduction from agnostic reliable learning to PUI yields negative reliable learners for these intersections with the same dimension dependence, for fixed smoothness. Finally, for PQ learning and testable learning with distribution shift, we prove qualitatively optimal SQ lower bounds of $d^{Ω(1/ε^2)}$, even for intersections of two halfspaces with Gaussian training data and arbitrary test distributions.
ai_summary: We introduce Gaussian partitioning, an algorithmic primitive for distributions smooth with respect to a Gaussian . It partitions space into polyhedral regions so that almost all mass lies in thin strips restricting a few orthogonal directions .

title: JHiMA-WebRL: A Joint Hierarchical Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Long-Horizon Web Tasks
abstract: Multimodal web agents have shown promising capabilities for interacting with websites through graphical user interfaces (GUIs), yet realistic web tasks often require long-horizon, multi-step planning that remains challenging for monolithic policies. Such agents must jointly infer high-level plans, navigate through intermediate states, track progress over extended interaction histories, and execute visually grounded actions. Although prior work has explored modular multi-agent systems with a separate planner, the planner is typically not updated jointly with the actor. We investigate whether explicitly separating and jointly training planning and execution provides a stronger inductive bias for long-horizon web navigation. We introduce JHiMA-WebRL, a joint hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning framework for web agents that couples a task decomposer with an actor. To train the decomposer, we use a strong teacher model to construct structured subtask supervision from multimodal GUI trajectories, and use these annotations to fine-tune both the decomposer and the subtask-conditioned actor. We then extend Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to jointly optimize the decomposer and actor in the interactive WebArena environment through hierarchical rollout grouping and role-specific advantages. On WebArena-Lite-v2, JHiMA-WebRL-14B, consisting of a 7B actor and a 7B decomposer, achieves an average success rate of 37.2%, compared with 24% for a ScaleCUA-32B agent that we fine-tune with RL on the same training tasks and evaluate under the same protocol. Ablations show that jointly updating the decomposer during RL outperforms updating the actor alone. These results suggest that jointly learned role factorization with smaller models can be a competitive alternative to scaling monolithic agents for long-horizon web tasks.
ai_summary: Multimodal web agents have shown promising capabilities for interacting with websites through graphical user interfaces (GUIs) Yet realistic web tasks often require long-horizon, multi-step planning . Such agents must jointly infer high-level plans and navigate through intermediate states .

title: NovoCRF: Globally Normalized De Novo Peptide Sequencing on a Prefix-Mass Lattice
abstract: De novo peptide sequencing has moved from dynamic programming over hand-designed or generative scores to large transformers that learn the task end to end. We present NovoCRF, a conditional random field (CRF) whose states are prefix masses, so that its paths are exactly the peptides within +/-0.06 Da of the precursor mass. A small network scores each edge from physics-derived ion-match features and is trained with its scores globally normalized over all mass-feasible peptides. To our knowledge, NovoCRF is the first de novo method trained with exact normalization over all mass-feasible peptides. Our software has three modules, each with exactly one job: a precursor mass finder recovers the accurate precursor mass from MS1, the CRF finds the peptides that fit the precursor mass by exact k-best decoding, and two BiGRU rerankers add sequence context and internal-fragment evidence. The model has 310k parameters and trains in about 17 GPU-hours. On seven held-out data-dependent acquisition datasets published in 2026 (126,262 labeled spectra), NovoCRF's mean peptide recall is 42.4%, against 39.1% for Casanovo v5 with five beams, and its amino-acid recall 64.0% against 53.1%, at 1,746 spectra/s on 18 CPU threads, 55x Casanovo's throughput on a GPU. Split by fragment evidence, NovoCRF leads on labels with up to three peptide bonds without a b or y ion, and Casanovo only beyond. NovoCRF can also search modifications it was never trained on at their exact mass: it finds 32.1% of the hydroxyproline peptides of a lion bone sample.
ai_summary: NovoCRF is the first de novo method trained with exact normalization over all mass-feasible peptides . The model has 310k parameters and trains in about 17 GPU-hours .

title: Going Deeper With Memories
abstract: Byte level language models avoid tokenizer dependence and provide universal coverage, but processing every byte at full resolution is expensive. We introduce DeepMem, a causal multiscale architecture that separates semantic compression from exact byte preservation. A learned invertible subband transform constructs a hierarchy of shorter sequences, while a lossless carrier and explicit detail sidebands preserve byte identity. Fast weight memory blocks operate along the encoder, with iterative shared state computation at the compressed bottleneck, while an attention based super resolution decoder restores byte resolution representations. DeepMem achieves stronger language modeling performance than a matched byte level Transformer on FineWeb-Edu and PG19, and obtains the best macro average performance across the evaluated FLORES languages. It also improves PIQA accuracy while remaining competitive on code modeling, multiple choice reasoning, and byte level corruption robustness. Bottleneck refinement requires approximately $7{,}600\times$ fewer counted FLOPs than equivalent full resolution reasoning, while maintaining competitive evaluation throughput.
ai_summary: DeepMem is a causal multiscale architecture that separates semantic compression from exact byte preservation . It improves PIQA accuracy while remaining competitive on code modeling, multiple choice reasoning, and byte level corruption robustness .

title: Logarithmic Regret for Alternating Mirror Descent
abstract: Alternating online mirror descent (AltOMD) is a simple learning rule for zero-sum games, which improves upon simultaneous OMD numerically and theoretically. Previous work obtained $O(T^{1/3})$ and $O(T^{1/5})$ regret bounds for AltOMD, by leveraging modified-energy-function-based analyses. However, settling whether AltOMD achieves near-constant regret has remained an open question. In this paper we resolve the question of whether AltOMD achieves near-constant regret in the affirmative. In particular, we show an $O(log(T))$ regret bound on the sum of the players' external regrets for any two-player zero-sum bilinear game with compact convex strategy sets, under mild regularity assumptions on the regularizers. We verify that our assumptions hold for the negative entropy regularizer, thereby obtaining logarithmic regret for the alternating multiplicative weights updates algorithm. The regret bound also yields an $O(log(T)/T)$ duality gap bound for the averaged strategies.

title: Shrinkage prior for implicit generative models
abstract: Implicit generative models based on deep neural networks have revolutionized many scientific fields, from weather research to language generation. They successfully model complex random objects arising in real-world problems. In this work, we propose a sample-efficient training mechanism for these models. Our approach leverages regularized inference with shrinkage priors and generalized Bayes. In the large $p$ (parameter dimension) and small $n$ (sample size) setting, sparsity-inducing priors have been successfully used for linear regression when $p \gg n$. However, their application to implicit generative models remains challenging due to the intractability of the likelihood function. To address this, we adapt a scoring rule posterior based on a strictly proper scoring rule, following the generalized Bayes framework. We then propose a block SGMCMC within Gibbs sampling mechanism. This enables efficient exploration of high-dimensional parameter spaces by identifying a sparse representation of neural implicit generative models. We demonstrate the performance of our proposed method through experiments on $p \gg n$ linear regression and an application of neural generative models.

title: Post-stratified importance sampling
abstract: Importance sampling is a building block of modern statistical computing, but the weighted estimate is prone to high or infinite variance. Moreover, its empirical standard error is often unreliable, leaving importance sampling without practical uncertainty quantification. Motivated by multilevel regression and poststratification (MRP) in survey sampling, we propose post-stratified importance sampling (PIS) for estimating target expectations from proposal draws. PIS reformulates arbitrarily high-dimensional weighting into two one-dimensional probabilistic modeling problems: regression for the conditional mean given the importance ratio and marginal density estimation for the importance ratio. Different modeling choices yield a family of PIS estimators, encompassing ordinary importance sampling as a special case. We develop a model-based implementation that combines one-dimensional Gaussian process regression for the conditional mean and score-informed heavy-tailed density estimation for the marginal law, using both the observed weights and the available density evaluations. We study the oracle gains of PIS and establish consistency under general and model-specific conditions. Simulations and applications to cross-validation demonstrate improvements in estimation accuracy and uncertainty quantification.
ai_summary: Importance sampling is a building block of modern statistical computing, but the weighted estimate is prone to high or infinite variance . We propose post-stratified importance sampling (PIS) for estimating target expectations .

title: ARLoop: Fully-Open Pre-trained Looped Transformers with Attention Residuals
abstract: Looped transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying a shared set of transformer layers, offering a parameter-efficient way to scale computation. However, standard residual connections aggregate information across recurrent depth into a single stream, providing limited control over which intermediate representations from preceding layers should be reused. In this paper, we introduce ARLoop, a looped transformer architecture based on attention residuals, where the input of each layer is selectively aggregated through attention over model depth. Distinct from standard transformers, we find that looped transformers do not require access to the full residual history: sliding-window depth attention matches or outperforms full-history attention at larger recurrent depths. Across controlled experiments with multiple parameter scales (140M and 370M) and recurrent depths (R = 1 to 5), ARLoop consistently outperforms prior residual designs for looped transformers. More importantly, we further scale ARLoop to 0.6B and 1.2B parameters under a realistic LLM pretraining recipe, demonstrating that the gains transfer to realistic pretraining, with particularly strong improvements on math and coding tasks. Our 1.2B model, pretrained on only 0.5T tokens with three recurrences, outperforms Huginn-3.5B (the only fully-open looped LLM as of our release date) across all evaluated tasks and is competitive with similar-sized non-looped models such as Qwen3.5-2B despite being trained on substantially less data.
ai_summary: Looped transformers increase effective depth by repeatedly applying a shared set of transformer layers . But standard residual connections aggregate information across recurrent depth into a single stream . In this paper, we introduce ARLoop, a looped transformer architecture based on attention residuals .

title: Cognitive demand as a neurometabolic stress test in diabetes-associated cognitive impairment: from static metabolite pools to dynamic energy responses.
abstract: Diabetes-associated cognitive impairment (DCI) is heterogeneous and cannot be explained by chronic hyperglycaemia or isolated resting metabolic abnormalities. Measurements of transporter abundance, metabolite pools, perfusion, or functional endpoints alone do not determine whether the brain can dynamically recruit energetic support when cognitive demand increases. To conceptualize cognitive demand as a neurometabolic stress test, distinguish static metabolic states from dynamic adaptive responses, and establish a falsifiable framework for activity-dependent neurometabolic failure in DCI. This concept-driven critical review used an iterative PubMed/MEDLINE-centred search updated through August 2026, supplemented by backward and forward citation tracking. Evidence was organized along the demand-to-function pathway, encompassing cognitive-task, glucose/insulin, hypoglycaemic or alternative-substrate, and neural/network challenges. Studies were prioritized when they provided information on temporal dynamics, pathway flux, cellular or regional specificity, or causal perturbation. Normal cognitive function requires coordinated recruitment of vascular delivery, substrate mobilization and allocation, oxidative metabolism, phosphotransfer buffering, and ATP turnover, even when metabolite and high-energy phosphate pools remain relatively stable. Evidence from diabetes and insulin resistance demonstrates heterogeneous, challenge-dependent abnormalities that may involve reduced response amplitude, temporal misalignment, altered substrate distribution, or impaired metabolic utilization rather than uniform cerebral hypometabolism. We propose four non-exclusive within-challenge phenotypes of neurometabolic failure: blunted recruitment, mistimed recruitment, substrate misallocation, and malutilization. Neurometabolic reserve denotes recruitable adaptive capacity; its exhaustion is considered a longitudinal contraction of that capacity, not a fifth within-challenge phenotype or a conclusion warranted by a single attenuated response. However, current evidence has not yet established a complete causal chain linking cognitive demand, substrate fate, energetic support, neural computation, and cognitive performance in clinically characterized DCI. We propose cognitive demand as an experimental neurometabolic stress test for investigating metabolic vulnerabilities that may remain undetected at rest, rather than as a validated clinical diagnostic test. Activity-dependent neurometabolic failure should therefore be considered a testable contributor rather than an established universal mechanism of DCI. Future studies integrating challenge-locked, temporally aligned, and compartment-resolved metabolic measurements with causal perturbation and longitudinal assessment are required to define when endocrine-metabolic dysfunction translates into cognitive vulnerability.

Measurements of transporter abundance, metabolite pools, perfusion, or functional endpoints alone do not determine whether the brain can dynamically recruit energetic support when cognitive demand increases .

title: Cone-beam CT-based synthetic CT generation for adaptive radiotherapy: methodological paradigms, clinical reliability assessment, and translation.
abstract: Synthetic computed tomography (sCT) generated from cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) has important applications in quantitative imaging, dose recalculation, and adaptive radiotherapy. Deep learning has improved image quality and Hounsfield unit accuracy, but its reliability for patient-specific dosimetry and routine clinical use remains uncertain. This narrative review examines deep learning methods for generating sCT from treatment CBCT in photon and proton radiotherapy, with emphasis on data requirements, generalizability, structural fidelity, dosimetric accuracy, and clinical feasibility. The literature search was last updated on 30 July 2026. Current methods mainly include supervised regression, adversarial networks, registrationguided approaches, and diffusion models. Available evidence demonstrates encouraging image and dosimetric performance, although no method consistently performs best across anatomical sites, imaging systems, and treatment modalities. Most studies are based on proof of concept or single-center validation and show considerable heterogeneity in datasets, acquisition protocols, reference images, registration methods, and evaluation criteria. External validation, prospective assessment, failure detection, and quality assurance remain limited. Future studies should emphasize multicenter validation, standardized and modality-specific evaluation criteria, uncertainty assessment, and prospective workflow testing. More rigorous and clinically relevant evidence is needed to support the reliable use of sCT in patient-specific adaptive radiotherapy.

abstract: Nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems have been proposed as a promising strategy for improving the efficacy and specificity of cancer therapeutics. However, predicting tumor delivery efficiency remains challenging because of complex interactions among nanoparticle physicochemical properties, biological environments, and experimental conditions. This study presents an explainable machine-learning framework for predicting nanoparticle tumor delivery efficiency using the updated Nano-Tumor Database. Following data preprocessing and feature engineering, 2,319 records were used to develop and evaluate Random Forest, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), weighted ensemble, and stacking ensemble models. title: Revisiting the MS paradox: automated 2.5D FLAIR segmentation and DTI microstructural profiling reveals dissociation between lesion burden and reference-like intralesional tract profiles.
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reveals macroscopic lesion burden in multiple sclerosis (MS) but correlates poorly with clinical phenotype, a phenomenon known as the clinico-radiological paradox. While diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) metrics assess microstructural damage, standard whole-lesion averaging may obscure microstructurally spared white matter within heterogeneous plaques. We propose a fully automated, multimodal pipeline to identify and quantify reference-like intralesional segments (RLIS) within MS lesions (i.e., the cluster exhibiting maximum feature-space similarity to subject-specific, lesion-spared reference tissue). A modified 2.5D U-Net, developed and evaluated on a cohort of 75 MS patients (115 series), performed automated FLAIR lesion segmentation. In an independent cohort of 100 MS subjects, intralesional DTI metrics (FA and MD) were extracted along streamlines reconstructed via Constrained Spherical Deconvolution tractography. Unsupervised clustering algorithms, validated against a subject-specific, lesion-spared reference CST streamlines (internal capsule), identified operationally defined reference-like segments. The 2.5D U-Net achieved robust segmentation performance (DSC: 0.732, VC: 0.954), exhibited higher nominal metrics in a contextual benchmark comparison (DSC: 0.682, VC: 0.864). Across the clinical cohort, lesion count (11-131) and volume (0.54-57.3 mL) varied widely. Among the evaluated clustering methods, K-Means and Gaussian Mixture Models proved to be the most conservative, identifying median reference-like segment proportions of 26% and 22%, respectively. Crucially, the proportion of reference-like intralesional segments showed no significant monotonic association with macroscopic lesion volume or count. This automated framework successfully integrates robust deep learning-based lesion segmentation with tract-specific analysis to quantify the proportion of reference-like intralesional segments. The observed dissociation between overall lesion burden and RLIS suggests that this index serves as a promising candidate metric for exploring microstructural features that may contribute to the clinico-radiological paradox.

title: Computational identification of EBNA1-binding candidates using machine learning-based virtual screening and molecular docking.
abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is associated with several malignancies and multiple sclerosis, and Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) plays an essential role in viral genome replication and episome maintenance. The experimentally characterized KVD-associated pocket within the EBNA1 DNA-binding domain provides a structurally defined site for computational ligand prioritization. This study aimed to identify and prioritize predicted EBNA1-binding candidates using an integrated machine-learning and structure-based virtual screening framework. A PubChem EBNA1 bioactivity dataset comprising 304,124 records was curated to obtain 4,584 unique compounds. Molecular representation combined 1,024-bit Morgan fingerprints with 11 RDKit molecular descriptors. Random Forest, SVM-RBF, Logistic Regression, and XGBoost models were evaluated using scaffold-based independent testing. The optimized XGBoost model was applied to a non-overlapping DrugBank library of 12,287 compounds. Compounds with predicted activity probabilities ≥0.5 were subjected to Lipinski-based filtering, followed by molecular docking against the KVD-associated binding pocket of EBNA1 (PDB ID: 6NPM). Docking validation was performed by independent KVD redocking at exhaustiveness values of 8, 16, and 32. Post-docking candidates were further evaluated using PAINS, aggregation, frequent-hitter/promiscuity, assay-interference, redox-associated structural-alert, and ADMET assessments. XGBoost demonstrated the highest test-set ROC-AUC (0.835), PR-AUC (0.408), and best Brier score (0.067), and was selected for virtual screening. Screening identified 116 compounds above the probability threshold, of which 40 satisfied Lipinski criteria and were docked. Thirty-two compounds achieved docking scores ≤ -7.0 kcal/mol. Sequential liability assessment and integrated prioritization identified 10 computationally prioritized EBNA1-binding candidates with favorable combined machine-learning, docking, and structural-filter profiles. The integrated computational framework enabled systematic prioritization of structurally diverse predicted EBNA1-binding candidates for further experimental investigation. The identified candidates represent computationally prioritized molecules for subsequent biochemical and functional evaluation of EBNA1 binding and activity and should not be interpreted as experimentally validated antiviral or disease-modifying agents. title: Rural digitalization and the multidimensional wellbeing of older adults in China: evidence from the active aging framework.
abstract: Building a more inclusive digital environment is a key strategy for promoting rural digitalization, narrowing the digital divide, and enhancing the wellbeing of older adults in rural areas. However, despite its increasing relevance, research on how rural digitalization affects the wellbeing of older adults in developing countries remains scarce. This study aims to examine the relationship between rural digitalization and the wellbeing of older residents in rural areas, with a particular focus on its underlying mechanisms and heterogeneous effects. Grounded in the World Health Organization (WHO) framework for active aging and the multidimensional measurement approach of the Active Aging Index (AAI), this study develops a comprehensive index for evaluating the wellbeing of older adults in rural China while accounting for the specific socioeconomic and contextual characteristics of rural areas. Using matched data from the China Provincial Digital Development Index (2016-2022) and the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), to systematically analyze the relationship between rural digitalization and the wellbeing of the older adults in rural areas, as well as the mechanisms underlying this relationship, and the underlying mechanisms are explored through a double machine learning approach. Analysis indicates that rural digital development significantly enhances self-efficacy, expands social networks, and strengthens social trust among rural older residents. These factors constitute key mechanisms through which digital development is associated with improved wellbeing among rural older residents. The heterogeneity analysis further reveals that the positive impact of digitalization on wellbeing are more pronounced among older adults with lower educational attainment, those with moderate or low income levels, and those living with their children, and the positive correlation is stronger in China's central and western regions. Overall, this study extends active aging theory to rural digital contexts in developing countries, thereby improving its contextual applicability, while also enriching the existing framework for evaluating the wellbeing of rural older adults and providing policy insights for promoting an inclusive digital society and a more equitable distribution of digital dividends.

title: Comparative analysis of GAN-based augmentation pipelines for Parkinson's hypokinetic dysarthria severity detection using deep learning.
abstract: Class imbalance is a common problem in speech-based severity detection, which can result in biased models and poor recognition of minority severity classes. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used for data augmentation, but very few studies have comparatively evaluated GAN-based augmentation at different stages of the speech-processing pipeline for assessing Parkinson's hypokinetic dysarthria severity. This paper compares GAN-generated speech (GGS) and GAN-generated image (GGI) augmentation methods for addressing class imbalance in low-frequency cepstrogram-based severity detection using the PC-GITA dataset. GAN-based augmentation was used to generate balanced training datasets using two different augmentation pipelines. The original speech and synthetic speech generated using GGS were converted into low-frequency cepstrogram representations, whereas GGI directly generated low-frequency cepstrogram images. These representations were used as inputs to a CNN trained and evaluated under Speaker-independent (SI) and Speaker-dependent (SD) conditions. In the speaker-independent evaluation, repeated five-fold speaker-stratified cross-validation with five independent random seeds yielded a mean accuracy of 56.47% ± 3.40% for GGS compared to 55.47% ± 3.35% for GGI and 53.13% ± 3.26% for the original-dataset baseline. GGS showed higher mean accuracy, precision, and specificity, whereas GGI showed higher mean recall and F1-score. In the speaker-dependent evaluation, GGI achieved the highest mean accuracy of 76.48% ± 4.09% compared to 73.04% ± 3.63% for GGS and 73.04% ± 3.25% for the original-dataset baseline. However, the speaker-dependent results represent an optimistic upper-bound evaluation because speaker identity was shared between the training and evaluation partitions. In general, the two GAN-based augmentation pipelines showed potential to address class imbalance under the conditions studied, while their relative performance depended on the evaluation protocol and the classification measure.

title: Smart materials and additive manufacturing for functional reconstruction in general surgery: responsive hydrogels, bioinks, patient-specific scaffolds, and translational validation.
abstract: Smart materials and additive manufacturing are transforming tissue engineering from passive replacement toward functional, responsive and patient-adapted reconstruction. General-surgical applications expose biomaterials to blood, bile, pancreatic enzymes, intestinal contents, polymicrobial biofilms, cyclic loading, hypoxia and inflammatory remodeling. These environments create failure modes that conventional sutures, meshes, drains and inert barriers cannot fully address, including leakage, infection, adhesion formation, fascial dehiscence, recurrent hernia, fistula, delayed vascularization and local tumor recurrence. This review evaluates stimuli-responsive hydrogels, wet-tissue adhesives, hemostatic sealants, antimicrobial and immunomodulatory matrices, decellularized extracellular-matrix bioinks, multi-material scaffolds, patient-specific printing and artificial intelligence-assisted design. Evidence is organized by surgical failure mode and operative workflow, with quantitative comparisons in abdominal-wall reconstruction, gastrointestinal anastomotic protection and hepatobiliary-pancreatic surgery. Material requirements also change with time: handling and hemostasis are determined within minutes, sealing and infection control within days, tissue integration over weeks and durable mechanics or degradation over months. We propose the GS0-GS5 validation hierarchy as a surgical translational framework that complements generic technology-readiness levels by linking each stage to wet and contaminated interfaces, organ-specific fluids, cyclic loading, standardized bench testing, and clinically scaled delivery. We argue that translation depends on treating each material as a procedure-specific system and reporting the linked material, processing and surgical metadata needed for reproducibility, regulatory assessment and clinical adoption.

title: Diagnostic and predictive value of structural and high-order functional brain topology in major depressive disorder.
abstract: Conventional neuroimaging analyses for major depressive disorder (MDD) predominantly construct brain networks based solely on pairwise regional functional couplings. Accumulating microscale neuroscientific evidence highlights the essential role of higher-order interactions (HOIs, interactions among three or more brain nodes) in capturing the intricate spatiotemporal dynamics of the human brain. This study aims to integrate machine learning techniques with neuroimaging topological features to systematically investigate the impact of non-pairwise interaction patterns in the brains of MDD patients on system dynamics, and to develop diagnostic and predictive models for MDD clinical manifestations. Firstly, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) data were acquired from 154 MDD patients with first-episode, drug-naïve and 153 age and gender matched healthy controls (HCs). Graph-theoretical analysis was applied to DTI-derived tractography data to quantify structural topology metrics, whereas persistent homology was adopted to extract higher-order functional topological signatures from rs-fMRI time series. Second, feature-level fusion was performed, and then a classification model was constructed using support vector machine (SVM) for MDD diagnosis. A repeated nested validation strategy with 50 repeated stratified 70/30 hold-out splits was adopted. Classification performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Subsequently, a prediction model was built based on the selected fused features using ridge regression, and the prediction performance was evaluated based on the correlation between the predicted values and the actual scale scores. Compared with HC, MDD patients exhibited significant alterations in structural and functional topological metrics within key brain networks, including DMN, VN and FPN. The classification performance of the SVM model integrating multimodal neuroimaging features achieved excellent classification performance, with an AUC of 88.2%. Additionally, multimodal imaging features demonstrated robust predictive capacity for suicide risk level in MDD patients (r=0.604). By integrating structural and higher-order functional topological features, we are able to effectively diagnose and predict MDD, highlighting the crucial role of higher-order interactions in the pathological mechanisms of brain networks in depression.
